prompt_context_by_prefix.consent:
Use these preferred technical term translations when relevant:
- count (tally): [needs translation sprint]
    DO NOT render as: the sense of MATTERING or being valued — "your visit counts", "make it count". This is a live English idiom and the most likely wrong reading; it turns a request for permission into a compliment; the sense of RELYING on somebody — "count on me"; the accounting or financial sense — an account, a balance, a reckoning of money; the noble title — count, as in a European rank. A real trap in Romance and Slavic languages, where the tallying verb and the title can share a root; rendering it as MEASURE or TRACK, both of which imply more than we do. We add one to a total; we do not measure or follow anybody
- cookie (browser storage): [needs translation sprint]
    DO NOT render as: the food — a biscuit, a sweet baked good. This is the literal meaning of the English word and the failure mode to expect, especially where the computing sense has not been borrowed; coining a descriptive phrase where your language already borrows 'cookie'. A visitor hunting for cookie settings will not recognise an invented term; widening it to all browser storage. The privacy notice distinguishes cookies from localStorage and IndexedDB deliberately, because they are listed as separate rows
- log (record): [needs translation sprint]
    DO NOT render as: the timber sense — a felled tree, a log of wood. This is the literal meaning of the English word and the failure mode to expect; the mathematical sense — logarithm. 'Log' abbreviates both in English, and in a suite full of engineering formulas this is a live confusion; the sense of LOGGING IN or signing in to an account. There are no accounts on this site at all, so any rendering that suggests one is wrong twice over; rendering it as MONITOR, TRACK or FOLLOW, all of which imply watching a person over time. We write one line saying a page was opened; we do not follow anybody; borrowing the English word where an ordinary verb for recording exists
prompt_context_by_prefix.lpn:
Use these preferred technical term translations when relevant:
- flow (Q): លំហូរ
- velocity (v): ល្បឿន
- head (H): ថ្ពល់
    DO NOT render as: a lazy anatomical calque that is NOT the language's natural hydraulic term — but an anatomically-derived word that IS the dominant local standard is correct (English 'head' is itself the body-part word repurposed); defer to the cultural standard, do not 'fix' a natural term for containing a body-part morpheme; pressure (head is a length/energy-per-weight, not a pressure); source/origin of a stream
- head loss (h_L): ការបាត់បង់ថ្ពល
    DO NOT render as: pressure loss / pressure drop (use the head-loss term, not the pressure term); a lazy anatomical calque that is not the local standard — an anatomically-derived word that IS the dominant standard is correct; see 'head' root entry
- friction loss (h_f): ការបាត់បង់ដោយកកិត
- minor loss (h_m): ការបាត់បង់មូលដ្ឋាន
- pressure (p): សម្ពាធ
    DO NOT render as: the HEAD term (a height of water column) — pressure here is what a gauge reads; atmospheric or meteorological pressure senses; a stress or material-strength sense; figurative 'pressure' (urgency, coercion)
- elevation (z): កម្ពស់
    DO NOT render as: the HEAD term — an elevation is a position above a datum, not an energy; a generic 'tall/high' adjective where the language has a surveying term; altitude in the aviation or geographic sense where a levelled survey term exists
- demand: តម្រូវការ
    DO NOT render as: economic or market demand; a legal demand/claim; a request in the everyday sense
- static head (H): សម្ពាធផ្គត់ផ្គង់ថេរ
    DO NOT render as: electrostatic / static electricity; 'stationary/motionless' in a non-hydraulic sense
- maximum allowable head (H): សម្ពាធអនុញ្ញាតអតិបរមា
    DO NOT render as: the operating / computed head (this is a fixed design limit, not the pressure the network actually develops)
- supply head (H): សម្ពាធផ្គត់ផ្គង់
    DO NOT render as: an economic 'supply'; confusing supply (source) head with the delivered/residual head at a demand point
- supply curve: [needs translation sprint]
    DO NOT render as: an economic supply curve; a demand curve
- looped network: បណ្ដាញបំពង់រង្វិលបិទ
    DO NOT render as: a control-flow / programming loop; a physical loop, knot, or coil
- branched network: បណ្ដាញបំពង់បែកសាខា
    DO NOT render as: a literal botanical 'tree' where the language has a proper network/graph term; a looped or meshed network (branched means no loops)
- pipe line: ខ្សែបំពង់
    DO NOT render as: a queue or line of people; a rope, cord, or cable; a line of text; a purely geometric line/segment
- pressure rating: សម្ពាធអនុញ្ញាតអតិបរមា
    DO NOT render as: a stress or material strength rather than a water pressure; blood-pressure or tyre-pressure senses; a general word for strong or high
- pressure reduction: ការកាត់បន្ថយសម្ពាធ
    DO NOT render as: naming a specific device (break pressure tank, BPT, pressure-reducing valve) as if the tool recommends one; depressurizing in the sense of emptying or draining the pipe
- energy grade line (EGL): ខ្សែថាមពល
- Manning roughness (n): ភាពក្រញ៉ោងម៉ាន់នីង
- friction factor (f): កត្តាកកិត
- draw (a diagram): [needs translation sprint]
    DO NOT render as: draw water (abstract, pump, or take water from a source) -- the wrong sense here, and PLAUSIBLE in a hydraulics context, which is what makes it dangerous; pull, drag, or haul; draw as in a lottery or a tie/stalemate; withdraw money
- junction: [needs translation sprint]
    DO NOT render as: a road junction, crossroads, or intersection; a physical pipe fitting (tee, cross, elbow) -- a junction here is a point in the model, not a part you buy; a railway junction; an electrical junction box
- reservoir: [needs translation sprint]
    DO NOT render as: a tank whose level changes over time -- lpn_ explicitly does NOT model tanks (see lpn_notes_2_def), and calling this one would promise time-varying behaviour that does not exist; a natural lake specifically, where the language has a general storage/supply term; a reserve or reservation in the non-physical sense
- node: [needs translation sprint]
    DO NOT render as: a computing/server node (a transliterated loanword where the language has a real graph or network-diagram term); a knot, lump, or swelling (the anatomical/botanical sense of the Latin root); a node in the wave-physics sense (a point of zero amplitude)
- link: [needs translation sprint]
    DO NOT render as: a hyperlink or web link -- the dominant modern sense of the English word, and the wrong one here; a chain link (the physical object); a connection in the social or logistical sense
- vertex: [needs translation sprint]
    DO NOT render as: a mathematical vertex of a polygon or a parabola apex, where the language has a plainer word for a bend or corner point in a drawn line; a peak or summit; a vertex in the anatomical sense (crown of the head)
- background image: [needs translation sprint]
    DO NOT render as: a backdrop in the theatrical/stage sense (the English source word was CHANGED to "background image" in Task 193 precisely to remove this transliteration lure); a wallpaper or decorative background; an online/satellite map layer -- this is a plain image file the user already has
- pump curve: [needs translation sprint]
    DO NOT render as: a curve in the geometric/road sense; a pump characteristic confused with an efficiency or power curve -- this one is head against flow
- project (saved network): [needs translation sprint]
    DO NOT render as: an engineering project or job in the contractual sense (a scheme, a works, a contract) -- this is a saved document; a projection (optical or cartographic); to project or forecast
- scenario: [needs translation sprint]
    DO NOT render as: a scene or setting in the dramatic/film sense; a scenario in the "worst case story" narrative sense, where the language has a modelling or variant-case term; a copy or duplicate of the network -- a scenario is a set of differences, not a second network
- zoom to extents: [needs translation sprint]
    DO NOT render as: a general "adjust/change the zoom" — this is the trap. es "Ajustar zoom" and pt "Zoom para ajustar" both shipped meaning ADJUST THE ZOOM, which describes the zoom slider, not this button. A verb meaning adjust/regulate/set is wrong unless the label also says WHAT is fitted; zoom in / zoom out / a zoom level or percentage — this command has no direction and no amount; a transliterated "zoom" loanword standing alone, where the language has a real word for showing the whole drawing; the photographic or camera sense of zoom (a lens movement)
- default (setting): លំនាំដើម
    DO NOT render as: the financial sense — failure to pay a debt, defaulting on a loan. This is the dominant everyday sense of the English word in many languages and the single most dangerous confusion here; the legal sense — failure to appear or to act, a default judgment; a bare "reset" or "restore" with the default concept dropped entirely. ro shipped calc_defaults as just "Reseteaza" (Reset) while its own calc_defaults_confirm used "valorile implicite" correctly — the button must say WHAT is restored; a word meaning normal/usual/ordinary where the language has a real settings term. sw shipped "maadili ya kawaida" (normal values) instead of "chaguo-msingi"; "kawaida" describes what is typical, not what the software ships with; the sports sense — winning or losing by default, by forfeit
- upstream: [needs translation sprint]
- downstream: [needs translation sprint]

consent.context: To add something to a running total. Used throughout the Task 286 consent banner (consent_body, consent_current_granted, consent_current_denied) and the privacy notice, where the whole ask is whether a visitor may be counted once rather than once per visit. The distinction the word carries here is VISITORS vs VISITS: a visitor is a person tallied once; a visit is a single page load. Use whatever ordinary verb your language uses for tallying or totalling; there is nothing technical about it, and the risk is entirely in the wrong sense being chosen.
consent.translation_notes: Created 2026-08-12 for the ROADMAP Task 286 consent banner, as the glossary half of a Wave 0 finding (dev/english-friction/251-lpn-26lang.json, key 'count'). Translations are deliberately EMPTY: this concept has an ordinary, settled verb in every language, we have no shipped values to attest, and inventing 26 of them would be exactly the judging-other-people's-terminology that CLAUDE.md forbids. The sprint fills them, and the mandatory glossary write-back records what each language actually chose. What the entry carries in the meantime is the part an agent cannot derive — which of the English senses is meant, and which four are traps.

consent.context: A small piece of information a website stores in a visitor's browser. Appears as the label consent_settings_link ("Cookie settings") — the control that reopens the consent choice — and throughout privacy.php. NOTE THE LABEL'S JOB: it must be the phrase a visitor or a regulator LOOKS FOR, so the conventional term in your language beats a more descriptive one. Most languages simply keep the English word 'cookie', and where that is the convention it is the right answer.

consent.context: To write down that something happened, in a file kept on the server. What EngCalcs logs is that a page was opened or a calculation was run — the page name, the language, and the time — with no IP address, no account and no identifier of any kind. Used throughout the Task 286 consent banner and privacy notice. The everyday verb your language uses for RECORDING an event is the right choice; there is nothing technical about it, and no language needs to borrow the English word.

lpn.context: Hydraulic head — energy per unit weight of water, expressed as a height of water column. The ROOT concept behind head loss, velocity head, weir head, and gross/net head. A length, never a pressure. Appears as a bare label in Weir Flow (ws_headWaterHeight), Orifice (or_head), and Manning Pipe Flow (mpf_velocity_head). Acceptable English synonyms (translate the concept, not the exact word): energy elevation, hydraulic grade line (HGL).
lpn.translation_notes: Newly seeded 2026-07-20 to close the long-standing gap where only the COMPOUNDS (head loss, velocity/weir/gross/net head) had entries but the root word 'head' did not — the root is what every agent re-derived (and sometimes mistranslated as anatomical head or pressure). Values below are the roots extracted from those compound entries and are best-effort/derived, not natively verified — confirm in the term-centric sweep (see ROADMAP). Several languages split the root by sense: the hydro-power 'fall' sense uses a different word than the pipe 'head' sense (cs spád vs tlaková výška; hr/sr visina·pad vs visina; ro sarcină vs cădere; tr yük vs düşü; ar علو/الارتفاع vs الضغط). Where that split exists, keep the pipe/energy-head root here and let the fall-sense compounds keep their own word. Slavic напор/напір, sw kimo (corrected from kichwa — see 2026-07-22 note below), and the هد/ہیډ/ہیڈ/हेड/ሄድ loanword family are consistent and documented across the suite (see 'head loss' notes). [2026-07-21 Task 128 RESOLVED — Tom decision] Native review is not realistically available for these; rely on AI guidance and defer to the locally natural term. Anatomically-derived head words are NOT inherently wrong (English 'head' is itself anatomical) — a blanket anatomical-head avoid was mistaken and has been reframed above. Accordingly: my or_head/ws_headWaterHeight 'ခေါင်းဆုံး' (contains ခေါင်း) is KEPT as a locally natural term — NOT a defect; the earlier ဖိမြင့်ဆင့် root is one acceptable variant, ခေါင်းဆုံး is another, both stand. he or_head/ws_headWaterHeight 'עומק' (depth) is KEPT as-is — for orifice effective head a depth-to-centroid reading is physically legitimate, and it is a natural term. This does NOT license reverting the documented cs/he/sw velocity-head calque fixes (rychlostní výška, עומד מהירות, kimo cha kasi): those were replaced because the anatomical word was not the natural term there, which the reframed avoid guard still forbids. hi: or_head uses शीर्ष, velocity-head same शीर्ष, root here is the हेड loanword — harmless internal variance, polish only. [2026-07-21 Task 131 tip sprint] Definitional tips now ship in all 26 languages on or_head/ws_headWaterHeight/mpf_velocity_head ('energy per unit weight of water, a height of water column, not a pressure' / 'kinetic energy as a height of water column'), anchoring the concept at point-of-use. am head re-verified CLEAN this pass: uses the ሄድ loanword, no ጭንቅ (distress) calque anywhere. my (ခေါင်းဆုံး) and he (עומק) or_head/ws labels CLOSED 2026-07-21 as locally natural (see Task 128 resolution above) — no label change made. Task 130 (2026-07-21): am odt_ keys (odt_h1, odt_notes_1_def) still carried the ጭንቅ (distress) calque for head, missed by earlier sweeps; fixed to ሄድ. [2026-07-22 sw head family → kimo, Tom + Kenya-engineer input] REVERSES 'sw kichwa': kichwa (body-part head) is NOT the Swahili engineering term for hydraulic head. Anchor — velocity head was already 'kimo cha kasi' (the accepted descriptive term), so kimo is the register's word for head and kichwa was a body-part calque. Applied across the sw lang file (mhp_gross_head, mhp_hl_check, mhp_notes_3_def, rc_notes_7_def, odt_notes_1_def, or_head + ws_headWaterHeight labels): head=kimo cha maji, head loss=upotevu wa kimo, gross=kimo cha jumla cha maji, net=kimo halisi cha maji, weir head=kimo cha maji juu ya kizingiti. Ride-alongs same pass: crown taji(royal)→kilele (or_ orifice crown; rc_ crest already kilele); weir kizuizi/bwawa→kizingiti cha maji ('water sill', incl. ws_/wi_ calculator identities, Lenye→Chenye noun-class agreement); specific gravity uzito maalum KEPT. RATIONALE: for the 0.65 low-resource languages engineering discourse happens in English (TZ/KE engineering education is English-medium); the local tongue lives at the field/extension register, so there is no fixed engineering-Swahili standard to defer to — descriptive clarity for a Swahili-speaking field worker is the goal, and TANZANIA is the specific target audience (Tom's Kenya engineer). See memory project_low_resource_register_reality. [2026-07-27 sw kichwa->kimo COMPLETED, ROADMAP Task 147] The 2026-07-22 decision above was only applied to the seven keys it named, leaving lib/lang.ec.sw.php split almost in half: 15 keys on kimo, 16 still on kichwa -- including the identity strings (menu + <title> + desc) of ALL THREE head-loss calculators (dw_, hw_, mphl_), which is the first thing a Swahili speaker saw. Found while closing Task 141. All 16 now converted: dw_/hw_/mphl_ main_menu+main_title+main_desc, mhp_hnet, mhp_notes_1_term, mhp_notes_1_def, mhp_notes_3_term, odt_h1, rc_Hp, ip_max_head. Head loss = 'Upotevu wa Kimo' (Title Case in identity strings, lowercase in prose, matching mhp_hl_check); net head = 'Kimo halisi' (parallel to mhp_gross_head 'Kimo cha jumla'). template_printable_title/_subtitle KEPT as Kichwa -- there it means 'title/heading', not the hydraulic sense. The swap was safe as a straight word substitution because kichwa and kimo are both noun class 7, so every cha/wa/kinacho- concord marker stayed valid. Verified: php -l clean, tag parity vs English on all 16, and back-translation of each. rc_Hp keeps 'bwawa' for weir (consistent with its already-converted sibling rc_notes_7_def); the ws_/wi_ kizingiti standardization is a separate concern. keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_2_def: Tanks, water quality, and control valves that open and close on their own (PRV, PSV, FCV) are not modeled. A pipe can carry a fixed minor loss, but not a valve whose open or closed state depends on the flow being solved for.
keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_3_def: Every project is a tab, and every tab is saved in this browser as you work. Clearing your browser data deletes them all, so keep your work in a file: File, Save as. An asterisk on a tab means it holds changes that are not in a file. Nothing is ever written to a file unless you ask. In some browsers a project connects to the file you save it to, and File, Save writes back to that same file from then on; in others no connection is possible, so Save is disabled and only Save as is available. When a project file is kept on a shared drive, this page tells you if a colleague already has it open, so that two people do not write over each other.
keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_5_def: A pump follows H = H₀ − aQ^b, where H is the head the pump adds and Q is the flow through it. Enter one, two, or three points from the manufacturer's curve. Three points — the head at zero flow, the normal working point, and the point of highest flow — fit H₀, a and b directly, and follow a published curve most closely. Two points fit a parabola (b = 2) with its peak at zero flow. One point uses a common rule: the head at zero flow is 1.33 × the head you enter, and the highest flow is 2 × the flow you enter, which again gives b = 2. A pump with no points entered adds no head at all. The curve is not cut off where the head reaches zero, so asking a pump for more flow than its curve can deliver gives a negative head. The fix is a bigger pump or a smaller demand, not a different curve fit.
keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_4_def: Scenarios, so that one project can hold several sets of demands. Tables of node and pipe results. Writing EPANET .inp files, so that a project can go back out to EPANET. Comments and suggestions are always welcome (see the feedback link above).
keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_epanet_def: In August 2026 the Hazen-Williams coefficient and exponent were changed to match EPANET. Head loss results differ from earlier versions of this page by up to 0.1 percent, which is far smaller than the uncertainty in the C value itself.

keys.lpn_notes_1_def: Solves one set of demands at a time, using the same global gradient algorithm EPANET uses. It does not model how the network changes over time.
keys.lpn_notes_2_def: Tanks, water quality, and control valves that open and close on their own (PRV, PSV, FCV) are not modeled. A pipe can carry a fixed minor loss, but not a valve whose open or closed state depends on the flow being solved for.
keys.lpn_notes_3_def: Every project is a tab, and every tab is saved in this browser as you work. Clearing your browser data deletes them all, so keep your work in a file: File, Save as. An asterisk on a tab means it holds changes that are not in a file. Nothing is ever written to a file unless you ask. In some browsers a project connects to the file you save it to, and File, Save writes back to that same file from then on; in others no connection is possible, so Save is disabled and only Save as is available. When a project file is kept on a shared drive, this page tells you if a colleague already has it open, so that two people do not write over each other.
keys.lpn_notes_5_def: A pump follows H = H₀ − aQ^b, where H is the head the pump adds and Q is the flow through it. Enter one, two, or three points from the manufacturer's curve. Three points — the head at zero flow, the normal working point, and the point of highest flow — fit H₀, a and b directly, and follow a published curve most closely. Two points fit a parabola (b = 2) with its peak at zero flow. One point uses a common rule: the head at zero flow is 1.33 × the head you enter, and the highest flow is 2 × the flow you enter, which again gives b = 2. A pump with no points entered adds no head at all. The curve is not cut off where the head reaches zero, so asking a pump for more flow than its curve can deliver gives a negative head. The fix is a bigger pump or a smaller demand, not a different curve fit.
keys.lpn_notes_4_def: Scenarios, so that one project can hold several sets of demands. Tables of node and pipe results. Writing EPANET .inp files, so that a project can go back out to EPANET. Comments and suggestions are always welcome (see the feedback link above).
keys.lpn_notes_epanet_def: In August 2026 the Hazen-Williams coefficient and exponent were changed to match EPANET. Head loss results differ from earlier versions of this page by up to 0.1 percent, which is far smaller than the uncertainty in the C value itself.
